dw-dossier.name: Dossier
dw-dossier.changelog:
2.5.1

Read this before updating a site that is paired with a DeadWatch account.

Changed: how "DeadWatch fleet access" starts. On a paired site where nobody has chosen, Dossier now accepts reads and changes from the DeadWatch account the site is paired with. In 2.5.0 such a site accepted nothing. This update switches it on for those sites. People and tokens in that account who hold the Dossier right can read the site's SEO data, and can change titles, descriptions, alt text, schema, the business profile and SEO settings through Dossier. The reason: an agency that pairs many sites should not have to sign in to each one first.

What a site administrator sees: a notice in wp-admin, on the dashboard, the plugins screen and Dossier's screens. It names the paired DeadWatch account and says what it may do, with one press to keep it, narrow it to reads and checks, or turn it off. The notice stays until an administrator chooses. The setup wizard asks the same on its Connect step.

To turn it off: press "Turn it off" in that notice, or go to Dossier, Settings, Advanced, MCP Server, "DeadWatch fleet access". To start a site on off before anybody signs in, add this line to wp-config.php before updating: define( 'DW_DOSSIER_FLEET_DEFAULT', 'off' ); The values read and write work too. A pairing zip cannot start a site wider than that line.

A saved choice always stands. A site set to off stays off, and a site set to reads and checks stays there. A site that is not paired accepts nothing, as before.

Not changed: only a signed request from the paired account gets in. A change still needs a person or token in that account that holds the Dossier change right, and "Allow write tools" not stored off. A call still reads only what a visitor could read. Turning off another SEO plugin and the export are still never run from DeadWatch.

Pairing zips: a zip made in DeadWatch can now carry off as a starting choice, as well as reads and checks or reads and changes. Dossier 2.5.0 does not store an off from a zip. A site paired that way on 2.5.0 accepts nothing while it runs 2.5.0, and starts on reads and changes when it is updated unless an administrator has chosen by then or the wp-config line is there.

A choice made before a site was paired again can only narrow what the new pairing gets: an earlier off stays off and an earlier reads and checks stays at reads.

Autopilot: on a site where fleet access stands at reads and changes, a person signed in to the paired DeadWatch account can start autopilot for it. That now includes a site on the default. A token cannot start it and no tool does. It still never covers turning off another SEO plugin. A grant started from DeadWatch stops counting when the site is paired again.

Correction to the 2.5.0 notes. They said nothing that comes through DeadWatch installs, updates, turns on or turns off a plugin. That is true of Dossier's tools and of this setting. It is not true of the pairing as a whole. DeadWatch can manage plugins and themes on a paired site through the connect library, which has its own box under Dossier, Settings, Connect: "Let this DeadWatch instance manage plugins and themes here". That box is ticked unless somebody unticks it. "DeadWatch fleet access" does not cover it.

Fix: two requests could save the autopilot record over each other, so a note saved by an agent could put back a grant a person had just ended. Every save now starts from a fresh read under a lock. Ending a grant never waits on that lock.

get-setup-overview, the site's report to DeadWatch and the tool list a site hands to DeadWatch now say where the mode comes from: a stored choice, the default, or wp-config. On a site where nobody has chosen, the tool list tells the agent so and asks it to get the operator's yes before each batch.

Full notes are in CHANGELOG.md.
